first.rationale:
The inherited memories are consolidated summaries, not source records: each states an outcome but none carries the caveats, sample scope, or follow-up horizon that would have been in the original experiment record. I treat them as generally reliable priors, not as settled fact, and spend the verification budget where it could actually change what I do.

Intended action is activation_messaging, so memory_91 is the memory my decision rests on and the first thing to verify. What I need from the archive is whether 'improved week-one engagement / first meaningful action' was measured only as a week-one proxy or whether it tracked through to retained, paying, qualified accounts. Activation-nudge effects are exactly the kind that look strong on a short-horizon engagement metric and wash out or invert by day 90; if the source record shows no downstream measurement, I keep this as a small guarded test with an explicit long-horizon readout rather than treating the lift as established.

Second verification is memory_86, chosen for a diagnostic reason rather than a confirmatory one. Onboarding was shortened on day 52; activation is down 6% and onboarding completion down 4% by day 76. Memory_31 (day 12) cut required signup fields and memory_86 (day 52) shortened onboarding, so the organization has now removed friction twice in the same funnel. A plausible reading of the current decline is not that we need more friction removal but that cumulative friction-cutting admitted lower-intent accounts, raising the denominator and depressing activation and completion rates. If the archived record for memory_86 shows the completion lift was rate-based without a matching lift in qualified downstream revenue, that reframes the whole situation and argues strongly against simplify_onboarding, which would otherwise look like the obvious fit for the declining metric.

I am deliberately not spending budget on memory_73. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing, but it is the candidate with the highest downstream value risk against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue: discount-acquired price-sensitive SMB accounts typically show weaker retention and expansion, and 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is precisely the phrasing that survives consolidation when the churn tail did not. I am declining it on priors, so verifying it would not change my action this week. Meeting a price attack with a price cut also concedes the axis of competition and is hard to reverse.

Referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist are reasonable but neither addresses the two metrics actually moving, and enterprise_sales_assist is a capacity-heavy bet to make on one week's slot.

Scale is small_guarded_test rather than standard_experiment: two of the three current signals are declines whose cause I do not yet understand, and committing broadly on top of an unexplained decline compounds the error. If verification shows memory_91 had genuine downstream measurement and memory_86 did not cause the current dip, I would scale up next cycle. Either way I want the readout instrumented on qualified revenue and retention, not week-one engagement alone, so the next agent inheriting this does not receive another caveat-stripped success summary.

final.rationale:
Verification did real work, and it partly went against me. My diagnostic hypothesis was that repeated friction-cutting (memory_31 on day 12, memory_86 on day 52) had admitted lower-intent accounts and mechanically depressed the activation and completion rates we now see falling. The source record for exp_86 does not support that: completion +13% came with time-to-value -2.1 days and 30-day retention +3%, which is the opposite signature from a denominator polluted with low-intent signups. I am dropping that hypothesis as the primary explanation and dropping memory_73 from my reasoning set entirely, since I never verified it and am not acting on it.

exp_91 also held up better than a consolidated summary would guarantee: week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, and critically 30-day retention +1% rather than nothing. That last number is what I was actually looking for. The lift is not purely a short-horizon engagement proxy; something survived to 30 days. It is a small something, and I want to be precise about that rather than let the word 'confirmed' do work it has not earned.

So I am committing to activation_messaging. It is the direct match to the largest moving metric (activation down 6% QoQ against a prior intervention that moved activation +6%), it has the only verified downstream signal among the candidates, and it does not concede the pricing axis to the competitor.

Two residual uncertainties keep this at small_guarded_test rather than standard_experiment. First, both source records stop at 30 days. Neither measures qualified revenue, expansion, or retention at 90 days, which is the horizon the stated objective actually cares about. A +1% 30-day retention effect is thin enough that it could be noise or could decay; I cannot tell from what the archive returned, and I should not pretend otherwise. Second, and more important: exp_91 ran in a different environment. It was consolidated on day 61, before a competitor entered with aggressive SMB pricing. A re-run now is not a replication — the account mix arriving in the funnel may have shifted, and an activation nudge that worked on organically-acquired accounts may behave differently on accounts that are simultaneously being courted on price. Confirmed-in-past-conditions is not confirmed-in-current-conditions.

I also still do not have an explanation for why activation and onboarding completion are both declining when the two interventions aimed at them verified clean. That unexplained gap is itself a reason for a guarded scale. Committing broadly on top of a decline I cannot account for compounds whatever the real cause is.

Instrumentation requirement, which matters as much as the action: read out on 90-day qualified revenue and retention alongside activation, segment by whether the account was price-shopping or competitor-exposed, and record the null and the caveats explicitly. Both memories I pulled were true but under-specified in exactly the way that made me spend budget to recover their horizon. I do not want to hand the next agent a third caveat-stripped 'confirmed.'
